script: My coworker asked me to hold the register for 10 minutes—then everything changed.. I just started a new retail job and today was my first day. I spent most of it on training modules, then the manager slid me to the register at the end of the shift. Clock‑out time was creeping up, so when the only other front‑desk person asked if I could hold the fort while she hit the break room, I said yes—just ten minutes, right? (I know, right?) Right after she left, the line exploded. I was juggling a long line and a lady who probably bought half the store, so I was feeling invincible. Then the assistant manager pops up and says, "Can you ring up these balloons for this guy?" Balloons—like, you can't just scan an inflated one. Each has a unique number, and this dude had a bunch of different ones, so I had to type them all in. I am in the middle of a customer when the manager asks if I can wait until I finish him. I say yeah—no big deal. I've handled a huge line, a mega‑spending lady, so how bad can this be? Then I look up. That guy—balloon buyer—gives me the most insane grin I've ever seen. "HEEERE'S JOHNNY." I am like, what the heck? He buys three cheap items, nothing big. Maybe he's just messing with me. But when I finish, he hands me a huge wad of change and I realize the horror: it's almost all nickels and a few dimes. He's got three customers behind him, including the balloon guy. Counting those nickels was a nightmare, especially since I am not a math whiz. He apologized later and we joked about it, but I still can't shake it. "What the heck, dude?" (Honestly, that was a lesson in how the audacity of the end‑of‑shift rush can turn a simple task into a circus.)
